episodes.190923: An MCV passing over Lake Erie and New York state helped to kick off scattered convection over northern and western Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours of June 17, 2024. In a very warm and humid airmass with moderately high CAPE but low shear, a few of these storms produced wind damage as they pushed into the Allegheny Plateau.
episodes.190960: Hot and humid lower levels under weak vertical wind shear promoted a couple rounds of widely scattered afternoon and evening showers and pulse thunderstorms across the Midwest.  A more organized cluster of convection tracked northward through southwestern Indiana during the early evening.  Here the combination of very high downward CAPE values around 1200 J/kg and strong boundary layer lapse rates set the stage for wet microbursts, with this potential being realized by the few strongest storms whose updrafts approached 30,000 feet above ground level.  Resulting damaging winds were confined to Vigo, Daviess and Martin Counties.
episodes.191182: A compact upper level disturbance moved across Lake Erie and into portions of the Finger Lakes region and into the Southern Tier of NY producing scattered thunderstorms late in the afternoon and early evening. The disturbance moved into an area with plenty of energy in the atmosphere, as well as capability to promote strong downdrafts. As a result, some storms produced locally damaging wind gusts across this area.
episodes.191212: A waterspout was spotted offshore of Panama City Beach. In addition, strong storms moving northwestward through Apalachee Bay produced strong wind gusts in excess of 34 knots along the coast as they moved inland.
episodes.191593: A lingering outflow from storms earlier in the day over Illinois was the focus for storms over Indiana, Michigan and eventually northwest Ohio. Severe weather reports in Ohio was limited to 1 inch hail.
episodes.191685: Thunderstorms developed along a semi-stationary front during the mid-morning and tracked northeast along the boundary through the late morning on Monday (6/17) across central and north-central Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced a brief tornado, damaging winds and small hail.
episodes.191873: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the western Nebraska Panhandle during the mid evening hours on 6/16, producing small to marginally severe hail before exiting the area.
episodes.192141: Destabilization and strong shear ahead of an approaching cold front led to the development of severe thunderstorms over portions of central Upper Michigan on the 17th.
episodes.192229: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the early evening hours and impacted portions of Frontier County. Later that evening, a line of thunderstorms developed over northern Nebraska. As this line dropped south, it produced thunderstorm damage around lake McConaughy and in the Mullen area.
episodes.192307: A warm front lifted through the region bringing a warm and moist airmass which produced thunderstorms.
episodes.192329: Scattered severe thunderstorms produced wind damage across portions of southeast Michigan.
episodes.192420: A pair of nearly stationary storms developed in Southwest Nebraska during the late afternoon into the early evening and produced hail stones up to 4 inches in diameter.
episodes.192662: There were several reports of damaging wind gusts on June 16th.
episodes.192728: With high pressure centered to the east, a weak disturbance lifted northward through the Quad State, producing clusters of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon into the evening in Southwest Indiana. One particularly robust downdraft blew off a barn roof and downed several trees south of Santa Claus. Elsewhere, wind gusts of 46 and 51 mph were measured near Melody Hill with an evening thunderstorm. Afternoon MLCAPE near 2000 J/kg decreased to 1000-1500 J/kg during the evening, while effective bulk shear was 20-25 kts.
episodes.192729: With high pressure centered to the east, a weak disturbance lifted northward through the Quad State, producing clusters of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon into the evening in Western Kentucky. Wind gusts were generally sub-severe, with the exception of a gust that caused a tree to split in Daviess County. Afternoon MLCAPE near 2000 J/kg decreased to 1000-1500 J/kg during the evening, while effective bulk shear was 20-25 kts.
episodes.192821: A wet period allowed for flooding to return to portions of the Little Sioux River. This was capped by a multi-day significant heavy rainfall event between June 20th through June 22nd which brought widespread rain totals between 5 and 10 inches with pockets in excess of 15 inches. As rainfall reached area streams and rivers, major to record flooding was observed, devastating several towns and communities. All river crest information is preliminary until made official by the gauge owner.
episodes.192834: A boundary, with favorable instability along with lift occurring as the nose of the low level jet move into the region, resulted in a line of showers and storms to develop as this boundary travelled across northern Iowa during the early morning hours of June 17th. This line of storms produced a few severe wind gusts across the far northern part of the state with values between around 60-70 mph, which also resulted in tree damage in Kossuth county.
episodes.192902: A brief stint of strong to severe thunderstorms developed in Perry County on the afternoon of June 17th under a strong ridge aloft and a prolonged heat wave at the surface. The unseasonably hot temperatures helped to spark thunderstorm development that afternoon, but the lack of assistance from passing disturbances resulted in convection to diminish fairly quickly. The resultant downburst winds caused downed trees in several communities within Perry County.
episodes.193026: An upper disturbance moving through an unstable air mass produced a few strong thunderstorms across portions of Lake Superior on the 17th.
episodes.193027: An upper disturbance moving through an unstable air mass produced a strong thunderstorm at Minneapolis Shoal Light on the afternoon of the 17th.
episodes.193127: Kentucky was in strong southwesterly flow after the passage of a warm front earlier in the day, and ahead of an approaching cold front. With a warm/moist airmass in place, it was no surprise that scattered showers and thunderstorms were present through much of the day, especially in the afternoon, for Kentucky and surrounding states. By the evening, a couple storms became strong enough that NWS Jackson forecasters warned them. Ultimately two reports of damage came out of the storms that moved through, one in Leslie County and one in Breathitt County.
episodes.193136: Intensifying high pressure suppressed an otherwise favorable convective environment. Strong daytime heating and southeasterly moisture advection off the Atlantic Ocean overcame the ridging to produce scattered showers and an isolated thunderstorm which caused wind damage in Bedford County.  In Roanoke, one storm passed across the city, producing a brief period of rain with rate in excess of 3 inches per hour.  The storm passed quickly however, with observed totals of between 1.25 and 1.5 inches.  FLASH 1-hour Average Recurrence Intervals spiked to between a 15-year and a 20-year event.  CREST Unit Streamflow briefly exceeded 500 cfs/mi^2.
episodes.193153: A convectively induced shortwave trough across southern Ontario province and eastern Lake Erie tracked across the forecast area. The trough, along with increased instability, caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop east of the Lake Erie lake breeze. Severe Thunderstorm Warnings, along with reports of related damage were confined to portions of the Western Southern Tier, Upper Genesee Valley and the Northern Finger Lakes.
episodes.193302: A couple rounds of thunderstorms in the vicinity of a warm front brought isolated large hail and damaging winds to portions of southern WI.
episodes.193332: On June 17th, a line of severe storms moved from southwest to northeast through portions of southeast Minnesota. As these storms progressed through the Rochester area, there were reports of both trees down and measured wind gusts of over 60 mph. Storms continued northeast into Wabasha County, producing isolated tree damage before crossing the Mississippi River into Wisconsin.
episodes.193333: During the morning of June 17th, a line of severe storms moved through portions of western and north-central Wisconsin producing wind damage and three weak tornadoes as it moved northeast.
episodes.193354: A very moist, tropical-like, airmass covered the Mid-South on June 17, 2024. A weak mid-level shortwave rotating around the western periphery of the upper-level ridge situated west of the Mid-South.  This feature interacted with the very moist and unstable airmass in place resulting in numerous showers and thunderstorms. A slow-moving heavy thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding in East Memphis.
episodes.193520: A lingering outflow from storms earlier in the day over Illinois was the focus for storms over Indiana, Michigan and eventually northwest Ohio. Several reports of downed trees and powerlines were received along with a hail report up to 1 inch in diameter.
episodes.193524: A lingering outflow from storms earlier in the day over Illinois was the focus for storms over Indiana, Michigan and eventually northwest Ohio. Several reports of downed trees and powerlines were received in the greater South Bend area.
episodes.193548: Thunderstorms erupted late evening on June 16 along a slightly elevated boundary with 2500-3500 J/kg MUCAPE and 30-35 knots of deep-layer effective shear.  Initial storms quickly became widespread along the boundary from south central to east central South Dakota and evolved into a large bow echo, which moved through southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa with numerous reports of damaging winds mainly along and south of Interstate 90.
episodes.193549: Thunderstorms erupted late evening on June 16 along a slightly elevated boundary with 2500-3500 J/kg MUCAPE and 30-35 knots of deep-layer effective shear. Initial storms quickly became widespread along the boundary from south central to east central South Dakota and evolved into a large bow echo, which moved through southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa with numerous reports of damaging winds mainly along and south of Interstate 90.
episodes.193550: A persistent tail of thunderstorms continued along the southern edge of a large convective system, resulting in prolonged rainfall over a couple hours across northeast Nebraska.  Rainfall amounts reached locally 3 to 4 inches (3.10 inches measured 2.5 miles northwest of Ponca) in the slightly hilly terrain around Ponca.
episodes.193609: With the effective frontal boundary forced well southward by overnight and early morning convection, only isolated elevated thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours.  The strongest cells produced hail up to quarter size with marginal elevated instability and effective shear around 30 knots.
episodes.193821: Isolated thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced strong wind gusts in the Qualla Boundary.
episodes.193828: On the edge of a large eastern CONUS ridge, thunderstorms developed despite the warm temperatures aloft as surface dewpoints increased to the low 70s and surface based parcels were able to overcome the ridge.
episodes.193829: On the edge of a large eastern CONUS ridge, thunderstorms developed despite the warm temperatures aloft as surface dewpoints increased to the low 70s and surface based parcels were able to overcome the ridge.
episodes.193832: On the edge of a large eastern CONUS ridge, thunderstorms developed despite the warm temperatures aloft as surface dewpoints increased to the low 70s and surface based parcels were able to overcome the ridge.
episodes.194131: Northern Ohio resided within the warm and humid sector along the northwestern flank of the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high during the late morning of the 17th through late evening of the 20th. In addition, a cold front drifted southeastward from the western Great Lakes to Lake Erie and northwest OH by the evening of the 20th.||Well-ahead of the the cold front, scattered multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted generally eastward or east-northeastward across northern Ohio during the early afternoon through early evening of the 17th and 18th, respectively. The ambient environment consisted of moderate to strong MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate effective bulk shear. Sporadic severe hail and straight-line convective wind damage occurred. Isolated flash flooding also occurred in northeast OH during the evening of the 18th. An isolated, slow-moving thunderstorm produced torrential rainfall across southeast Trumbull County, which led to localized flash flooding. Two rounds of thunderstorms across Lake County produced minor flash flooding due to intense rainfall rates. ||Isolated multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted generally northeastward or eastward across northwest OH during the early evening of the 19th and 20th, respectively. The ambient environment consisted of moderate to strong MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate effective bulk shear. These storms produced sporadic small hail and straight-line convective wind damage.
episodes.194226: Lake Erie resided in the warm and moist sector along the northwestern flank of the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high pressure ridge during the early evening of the 17th through early evening of the 18th. Simultaneously, a surface front, oriented from northeast to southwest, remained nearly-stationary across the Upper Midwest. Isolated multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted eastward across western Lake Erie during the early evening of the 17th and generated gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the northwest OH shore. During the early to mid-afternoon of the 18th, scattered multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted generally eastward over and near central and eastern portions of Lake Erie. These storms generated peak convective wind gusts of gale-force to storm-force along the northeast OH shore. All of these storms occurred in an ambient environment with moderate to strong MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.195532: A thunderstorm complex moved across southern Minnesota early Monday morning. These  storms produced severe winds with several measured gusts near 60 mph.
